title: Support for women’s reproductive autonomy is broad, but access and abortion legitimacy remain conditional on age, marriage, and circumstance
source_unit: Afrobarometer, East Africa sexual and reproductive health and rights news release, Round 10
geography: Comoros, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Mauritius, Madagascar, and Seychelles; 2024–2025 surveys

denominator.unit: interviews across seven East African countries

marriage_autonomy.unit: percent agreeing women and girls should decide for themselves whether and when to marry

childbearing_autonomy.unit: percent agreeing women should decide for themselves how many children to have and when

cross_country_support.value: Majorities supported both forms of autonomy in all seven surveyed countries

autonomy_boundary.value: Support for decision-making autonomy is broad, but the survey does not measure whether women can exercise it safely or access services needed to do so

observations.method: Afrobarometer Round 10 face-to-face interviews in respondents’ language, nationally representative within seven countries, weighted equally for the multi-country average, with margins of error of approximately plus or minus 2–3 percentage points at 95% confidence.
observations.uncertainty: Sensitive questions may generate non-response or social-desirability bias; opinions are not observed reproductive behavior, service access, or household decision-making power.
observations.subgroup: Citizens across seven East African countries, with country-level variation and smaller subgroup uncertainty.
observations.counterinterpretation: Respondents may endorse autonomy as a general principle while accepting family, religious, economic, or legal constraints in actual decisions.

denominator.unit: interviews across seven East African countries

sexuality_education.unit: percent endorsing sexuality education in schools

contraception_marital_status.unit: percent saying contraceptives should be available to sexually active people regardless of marital status

contraception_age.unit: percent saying contraceptives should be available regardless of age

access_layering.value: Support for school-based information and marital-status-neutral access is higher than support for unrestricted age-neutral access

observations.method: Weighted multi-country survey with separate questions on sexuality education, contraceptive access by marital status, and contraceptive access by age.
observations.uncertainty: The questions measure public norms and policy preferences, not actual service availability, provider practice, affordability, confidentiality, or adolescent access.
observations.subgroup: Citizens across seven countries, including adults with different views on marriage, age, sexuality education, and reproductive health.
observations.counterinterpretation: Respondents may distinguish education from service access, or express concern about safeguarding and age without opposing contraception for adults or married people.

denominator.unit: interviews across seven East African countries

health_life_risk.unit: percent saying abortion can always or sometimes be justified when the woman’s health or life is at risk

rape_incest.unit: percent saying abortion can always or sometimes be justified when pregnancy results from rape or incest

economic_hardship.unit: percent saying abortion can always or sometimes be justified when the woman cannot economically care for a child

unwanted_pregnancy.unit: percent saying abortion can always or sometimes be justified when the woman does not want the pregnancy for any reason

circumstance_gradient.value: Support is substantially higher for health-risk circumstances than for economic hardship or an unwanted pregnancy without another stated justification

observations.method: Survey vignette-style questions asking whether pregnancy termination can always, sometimes, or never be justified under four circumstances.
observations.uncertainty: Justification attitudes are not legal status, service access, personal behavior, or clinical judgment; wording and social desirability may affect responses, and country variation is substantial.
observations.subgroup: Citizens across seven East African countries, with country-level and demographic variation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Respondents may support legal or ethical exceptions without supporting unrestricted access, or may interpret economic and autonomy scenarios differently across national contexts.

observations.period: 2024–2025; cultural legitimacy, education, and reproductive health policy

denominator.unit: East African countries with comparable sexual and reproductive health and rights survey modules

country_range.value: Support for sexuality education exceeded 90% in Madagascar, Mauritius, and Seychelles and did not fall below 60% in any surveyed country

service_legitimacy_gap.value: Public endorsement of autonomy and education exceeds support for every form of unrestricted contraceptive or abortion access

institutional_route.value: Schools, health services, families, religious and community norms, and law jointly shape whether autonomy becomes usable reproductive agency

voice_without_delivery.value: High stated support creates a public mandate signal but does not establish that institutions provide safe, confidential, affordable, or equitable care

observations.method: Comparative interpretation of the Afrobarometer survey modules and country-level distributions, retaining opinion, institutional, and service-delivery layers as distinct.
observations.uncertainty: This is a synthesis of cross-sectional public-attitude measures; it does not estimate institutional capacity or causal effects of sexuality education or legal reform.
observations.subgroup: Women and girls, adolescents, sexually active people, families, schools, providers, and policymakers across seven countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Public support may not translate into policy change where elite vetoes, provider constraints, funding shortages, stigma, or legal and religious institutions limit implementation.

related_sources.claim: Afrobarometer identity, society, and gender topic context.
Afrobarometer health, education, and social-services topic context.

boundary: This record adds East African public-attitude evidence on marital autonomy, childbearing decisions, sexuality education, contraceptive access, and abortion justification. It preserves the distinction between cultural norm, policy preference, law, service availability, and lived reproductive agency; it does not measure behavior, clinical outcomes, legal compliance, or institutional delivery.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Afrobarometer five-page news release reviewed for seven-country sample, 12,000 interviews, margins of error, equal country weighting, autonomy, sexuality education, contraception, abortion circumstances, and sensitive-question limitations.
